{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "josibake",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Strong Concept ACK endorsing in-house customizable test runner"
    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected to fallback printing type names; suggested dropping guix workaround and handling optional stringification"
    },
    {
      "login": "fanquake",
      "stance": "question",
      "note": "asked why Boost library instrumentation was relevant given Boost has been header-only"
    },
    {
      "login": "jeanpablojp",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK, but raised multiple behavioral regressions and bug reports"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:3571556207",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Silently printing mangled or compile-time type names at runtime instead of failing compilation when formatting is missing loses compile-time safety and differs from master.",
      "quote": "This should remain a compile failure, like it is on current master.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added static_assert and CHECK_NO_DISPLAY macro",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3577755372",
        "rc:3578111730",
        "rc:3579556440",
        "rc:3588808596",
        "rc:3614281814"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3595340862",
      "status_by_quote": "CHECK_NO_DISPLAY sounds fine. The benefit of the static assert is that it can print the problem and solution at compile"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3577321667",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "How could Boost library missing instrumentation cause issues when Boost has been header-only since #24301?",
      "quote": "not sure how the library missing instrumentation could be the cause of issues here?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author verified CI and dropped the commit",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3577492827",
        "rc:3578675788"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3578675788",
      "status_by_quote": "Looks like an older state of the framwork or commit history was causing this, dropped the commit."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5128275849",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Drop the unused boost workaround in guix.",
      "quote": "Could rebase and drop the unused boost workaround in guix?",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author removed the unused Boost workaround in guix",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5128275849",
      "status_by_quote": "Could rebase and drop the unused boost workaround in guix?"
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5061768134",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Dropping BOOST_TEST_RUN_FILTERS causes test coverage scripts to run the whole test suite instead of specific suites.",
      "quote": "BOOST_TEST_RUN_FILTERS is no longer read, so deterministic-unittest-coverage runs the whole binary instead of the suite it was given.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author re-added filter support",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5618550287"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5618550287",
      "status_by_quote": "Fixed"
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5061768134",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Dropping Boost.Test flags causes downstream CI scripts like libmultiprocess to fail immediately.",
      "quote": "bitcoin_core_ci.sh in the libmultiprocess subtree still passes three Boost.Test flags, and any one of them now makes it exit with code 2 without running anything.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added compatibility flags and separated summary from log level",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5618550287"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5618550287",
      "status_by_quote": "I added a catch_system_error flag for compatibility as well as a separation between the summary and log level."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5061768134",
      "part": 3,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "Should unit tests covering failure paths in framework.h be added or left for a follow-up?",
      "quote": "That's 1096 new lines in framework.h and I couldn't find anything covering their failure paths. util_check_tests covers both paths for Assert. Would something similar work here, or is it worth a follo",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390075",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Comparing null C-strings segfaults rather than reporting a test failure.",
      "quote": "With either side null this segfaults instead of reporting the failure.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added null check before strcmp",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978611293"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3978611293",
      "status_by_quote": "Added a check if either side is null so it does not go through strcmp"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390077",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Unflushed output causes test logs before a crash to be lost when output is redirected.",
      "quote": "This never flushes. With a crash inside a test case and output redirected, master keeps the preceding lines and here the file comes back empty.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added cout flush",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978604713"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3978604713",
      "status_by_quote": "I think a cout flush should solve these. Updated in latest push."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390077",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Unflushed output causes duplicate output on child process exits when tests fork.",
      "quote": "The same buffer causes a second, smaller thing. test_LockDirectory forks and the child exits with exit(0), reprinting what it inherited, so the output comes out duplicated.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added cout flush",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978604713"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3978604713",
      "status_by_quote": "I think a cout flush should solve these. Updated in latest push."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390078",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Dropping the entire guix linker block drops -Wl,--fatal-warnings from all Linux builds instead of only dropping the riscv64 exception.",
      "quote": "Dropping the whole block means no Linux host links with -Wl,--fatal-warnings any more, while build_win.sh and build_win_gui.sh keep it.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author re-added -Wl,--fatal-warnings",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978584583"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3978584583",
      "status_by_quote": "Added Wl, --fatal-warnings on head commit, lmk if thats what you mean"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390082",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "BOOST_TEST_RANDOM is treated as a boolean without parsing the seed value or logging the used seed, making test run ordering non-reproducible.",
      "quote": "Here the value is only checked for presence, never read, so 0 and an empty string both turn shuffling on and a fixed seed no longer reproduces.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author fixed seed handling and printing",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978594424"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3978594424",
      "status_by_quote": "Fixed by using a random seed and printing it if equal to 1, and setting the seed directly if > 1."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390086",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Comparing two optional<T> without operator<< bypasses static_assert and prints type names instead of failing compilation.",
      "quote": "This overload wins over the primary by partial ordering, so the static_assert never reaches std::optional.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "author noted they are still figuring out what to do",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6160640408"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "c:6163495505"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3890390092",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "TEST_CASE inside a TEST_SUITE does not run the suite fixture, deviating from Boost and the PR description.",
      "quote": "TEST_SUITE_BEGIN(suite, Fixture) sets btc_suite_fixture, but TEST_CASE registers a plain function and never uses it.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author updated TEST_CASE to use suite fixture",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3978601459"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3978601459",
      "status_by_quote": "Seems fine. I would think it very strange to update a global as part of a test fixture, but this is a code reduction and"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6163495505",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Separate stringify for optional truthiness checks from stringify for optional value comparison checks.",
      "quote": "would it be possible to have a `stingify_optional_truthy` which is called on truty checks and a separate `stingify_optional`, which is called on value cmp checks?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author agreed with the idea",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:6163538944"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6163538944",
      "status_by_quote": "Yeah I was thinking something along those lines"
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:4959035820",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Having an in-house customizable test framework removes barriers to writing tests and enables concurrency improvements to speed up CI.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5061768134",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "The whole suite passes and the scripted-diff reproduces cleanly.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "both",
      "areas": [
        "framework.h"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "resolving std::optional<T> compilation failure vs truthiness stringification",
      "id": "rc:3890390086"
    },
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "answering whether unit tests for failure paths in the framework are needed",
      "id": "r:5061768134"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Author pushed updates separating framework into .h and .cpp, and acknowledged rc:3890390086 regarding optional<T> is still pending. maflcko suggested a split stringify approach which the author agreed with."
}
